title: Browser Automation Playbook
subtitle: Production Engineering Edition
author: Yasaka Hanini
description: An enterprise-grade handbook for building reliable, self-healing browser automation pipelines. Covers raw Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) manipulation, resilient containerization, advanced anti-bot evasion, and system recovery workflows.
formats: Docker Compose templates for headless clusters
Standalone Production Reference Library & Failure Case Studies

changes: 392 pages across 14 chapters, including a full Production Reference Library.
Renamed incident headings to 'Production Incident' and analysis to 'Engineering Analysis' across all chapters.
Added advanced chapters on Shadow DOM, virtualized lists, Docker Compose, and memory drift daemons.

faqs.q: What browser and tools are used in this playbook?
faqs.a: This playbook focuses on asynchronous Python automation using 'nodriver' and direct raw Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) integration, bypassing high-cost driver layers.

faqs.q: What is the 'Production Reference Library' mentioned in the product description?
faqs.a: It is a standalone, curated PDF set of 20 post-mortem analysis reports, failure scenarios, and design review checklists summarizing five years of real-world enterprise browser automation incidents.

faqs.q: Do I need to buy Book 1 first?
faqs.a: No, Book 2 stands on its own. While Book 1 (Cookbook) is recipe-oriented for specific tasks, Book 2 (Playbook) focuses on the system architecture, reliability engineering, and infrastructure scaling required to run hundreds of headless browsers unattended in production.
